create.name: Sister Joan Chittister
create.bio:
Sister Joan Chittister is a Benedictine nun of the Erie community in Pennsylvania, an author and speaker whose writing draws on the monastic tradition to speak to ordinary lives. She led her community as prioress for twelve years and has headed two national bodies, the Leadership Conference of Women Religious and the American Benedictine prioresses' conference. She earned a doctorate in communications at Penn State, which now keeps the main collection of her papers.

Over five decades she has written more than sixty books along with a long-running column for the National Catholic Reporter, and her work keeps returning to the Rule of Benedict: silence, humility, community and attention to the present. Recent titles include The Monastic Heart, a set of fifty everyday contemplative practices; Radical Spirit, which reads Benedict's ladder of humility as a way to a freer life; and Between the Dark and the Daylight, on living with life's contradictions. She is executive director of Benetvision, a centre in Erie for contemporary spirituality, and the guiding voice of Monasteries of the Heart, an online community for people seeking a monastic rhythm outside a monastery. She also sends out The Monastic Way, a free monthly set of daily reflections, and has twice been Oprah Winfrey's guest on Super Soul Sunday.

books.title: The Monastic Heart: 50 Simple Practices for a Contemplative and Fulfilling Life
books.author: Joan Chittister
books.description: Fifty short chapters on building an inner monastery: simple daily practices drawn from Benedictine life for anyone, anywhere.

books.title: Radical Spirit: 12 Ways to Live a Free and Authentic Life
books.author: Joan Chittister
books.description: Benedict's twelve steps of humility retold as a path out of busyness and striving towards a simpler, more honest life.

books.title: Between the Dark and the Daylight: Embracing the Contradictions of Life
books.author: Joan Chittister
books.description: Short reflections on the quiet hours between night and day and what life's paradoxes can teach the soul.
